text: The Anthem of Bogotá is the musical composition that symbolizes the capital city of Colombia. It was officially adopted through Decree 1000 of July 31, 1974. The lyrics were written by poet Pedro Medina Avendaño and the music was composed by musician Roberto Pineda Duque. The anthem was selected through a public concourse announced following Agreement 71 of September 9, 1967, whose judge was named by Decree 731 of July 3, 1974, and the prize was 50,000 pesos. The judges of the concourse selected the song on July 31, 1974, and Mayor Anibal Fernandez de Soto signed the decree declaring it the official anthem of the city. Its debut took place on August 7, 1974, in a concert held at the Jorge Eliecer Gaitan Theater. Agreement 1 of April 19, 1988, establishes the rules for the use of the symbols of the city of Bogotá. Decree 120 of March 14, 1991, requires citizens to teach the city's symbols in educational centers and to sing the anthem at every public event within the city. Finally, Decree 64 of February 12, 1993, mandates every educational establishment to raise the city's flag weekly along with the intonation of the anthem. Since the enactment of this decree, some football fans have sung the anthem at every sports event, which helps promote its learning among the youth of the city. The lyrics include the lines: "a tu tierra y tu puro vivir, blanca estrella que alumbra en los Andes, ancha senda que va al porvenir," "a una espada, a una cruz y a un pendón. Desde entonces no hay miedo en tus lindes, ni codicia en tu gran corazón," "el cordaje de un nuevo laúd, y hoy se escucha el fluir melodioso en los himnos de la juventud," "que sonríe ante el vano oropel, siempre atento a la luz del mañana y al pasado y su luz siempre fiel," "una alfombra tendida a tus pies y del mundo variado que animas eres brazo y cerebro a la vez," "de un imperio sin puestas de sol, en ti un templo, un escudo, una reja, un retablo, una pila, un farol," "y a Bolívar, que torna a nacer; a Nariño, accionando la imprenta, como en los sueños los vuelves a ver," "tantos hombres de fama inmortal, que en el hilo sin fin de la historia les dio vida tu amor maternal," "Caros, Cuervos, and Pombos and Silvas, so many men of eternal fame, that in the endless thread of the history they were given life by your maternal love," and "en la patria no hay otra ni habrá. Nuestra voz la repiten los siglos: ¡Bogotá, Bogotá, Bogotá!."
